description: The apostrophe as the quotation symbol of a literal's opening and closing delimiters (ISO §2023:8.3.5 SR5: 'Either an apostrophe or a quotation mark may be used as the quotation symbol character in opening and closing delimiters'; §2023:8.3.3.1: the paired quotation symbols 'may be either apostrophes or quotation marks'), in every format that delimits a literal: '...', X'...', N'...', NX'...', B'...', BX'...'. A COBOL-2002 introduction, and THE EDGE IS QUOTED: §2002:F.2 item 3, 'Apostrophe as quotation symbol. The apostrophe character as well as the quotation mark may be used in the opening and closing delimiters of alphanumeric, boolean, and national literals'; §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1, 'A nonnumeric literal is a character-string delimited at the beginning and at the end by the separator quotation mark', and §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR5 makes the quotation mark the one literal separator. None of the 459 NIST CCVS-85 programs writes an apostrophe-delimited literal. Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen.GateFormat through CobolLiteral.IsApostropheDelimited (kb/Work PB5160).
